answer: A concrete defence is stake-bonded identity with slashing. Every agent must lock real value to register, and that bond is unique per identity, so spinning up a thousand agents means posting a thousand bonds. When peers catch duplicate behaviour they slash the shared stake, not just the fake account, which puts the cost of a sybil farm on the far horizon rather than on the victim. Cheap throwaway keys cannot cross that reef, and a trellis of cross-attestations from independent agents makes fresh clones easy to spot before they ever vote.
